reflection: Which of the three descriptions fits you most closely: burnout, spiritual dryness, or emotional overload? Which fits least?
How long has this been going on? When did you first notice?
Is there a specific event you can connect it to (a loss, a move, a conflict, a change of role), or did it build gradually with no obvious cause?
If the check-in pointed you toward support, who will you contact, and when?

checkin.title: Personal Readiness Check-in
checkin.intro: This is not a test and it is not scored. It helps you notice what deserves attention, and it may point you toward support before you begin. Your answers are for your personal reflection. They are not monitored in real time, and completing this check-in does not contact anyone on your behalf. If you are in immediate danger, call your local emergency number now.

sections.question: What have you experienced during the past month? Mark everything that applies.

options.text: Difficulty functioning at work or home
Thoughts of wanting to disappear or not be alive

sections.question: How long has this been happening?
How much is it affecting ordinary life?

options.text: My work, relationships, sleep, eating, or self-care are significantly affected
I am struggling to manage ordinary responsibilities
I am struggling to remain safe

sections.question: Do you feel safe being alone for an extended period?

guidance.heading: Please get support before anything else
guidance.text: One or more of your answers suggests that this is more than tiredness, and that being alone in silence may not be safe for you right now. That is not a failure of faith, and it does not mean the retreat is closed to you. It means the order matters: help first, retreat later. Tell a trusted person today, and contact a doctor, a qualified mental-health professional, or a crisis service where you live. If you believe you may act on thoughts of not being alive, or cannot keep yourself safe, contact your local emergency number or go to the nearest emergency department now, and ask someone to stay with you.

guidance.heading: Speak with a doctor or counsellor before you retreat
guidance.text: What you describe has lasted two weeks or longer and is affecting ordinary life, or has reached the point where ordinary responsibilities are hard to manage. That is the point at which a pastoral description stops being enough. Please make an appointment with a doctor or a qualified mental-health professional before you begin, and tell them you are planning this retreat. Choose path 2 (proceed with support), 3 (an adapted format) or 4 (postpone) in Lesson 5. The retreat will still be here.

guidance.when: alone_in:uncertain OR impact_in:some,significant OR duration_in:over2w,months,unsure OR signs_count_gte:4
guidance.heading: Consider a gentle, supported format
guidance.text: Your answers suggest you are carrying a good deal. You can still take this retreat, but plan it with support: tell someone what you are doing, arrange contact during the retreat, and consider a shorter or at-home format rather than three days alone. Lesson 5 will help you choose the right path, and Module 3 has the shorter formats. If things get worse before you begin, or you start to feel unsafe, seek help first.

guidance.heading: You look ready to prepare
guidance.text: Your answers suggest tiredness rather than crisis. Carry on with the preparation lessons, be honest in the reflections, and tell at least one person about the retreat. If anything changes before you begin, come back and do this check-in again.

checkin.notes: Apply guidance in `priority` order; the first rule whose `when` matches wins. `urgent` overrides everything: show its text and CTA, hide the ordinary Continue/next-lesson link and the lesson's next-step checkbox, and show the Finding Help link instead.
